public_rationale: Marcus accurately summarizes the reported scaling trend. The study examined different-sized versions within model families as well as pooled size groups, and its researchers report stronger covert prejudice in larger models. The evidence supports that bounded finding, not an unrestricted claim that increasing parameters must always increase racism.
limitations: The decisive quotation is a researcher interview in an institutional report; the underlying primary study was also read.
Pooling model families and using existing checkpoints limits isolation of parameter count as the sole cause.
The result does not establish a universal or strictly monotonic scaling law.

from_speaker: scale actually makes the covert racism worse
our_interpretation: In this study discussion, 'scale' means model parameter count and 'worse' means stronger negative dialect associations.
The claim is read as a trend within the examined models, including comparable sizes within model families. It is not a universal law covering every future model or training method.
The reference to Birhane is background attribution, not a separate claim being graded.
criteria.support_condition: Comparisons involving otherwise comparable model sizes show stronger covert dialect prejudice as size increases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable scaling comparisons show consistently weaker covert prejudice, or demonstrate that the reported worsening disappears when model-family differences are accounted for.
